questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Group I contains three broad classes of irrigation supply canal outlets. Group II presents hydraulic performance attributes.
Group IGroup II
P. Non-modular outlet1. Outlet discharge depends on the water levels in both the supply canal as well as the receiving water course
Q. Semi-modular outlet2. Outlet discharge is fixed and is independent of the water levels in both the supply canal as well as the receiving water course
R. Modular outlet3. Outlet discharge depends only on the water level in the supply canal
The correct match of the items in Group I with the items in Group II is
questions.explanation:
Irrigation Engineering | Canal Distribution Systems

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Group I containing classes of canal outlets (Non-modular, Semi-modular, Modular) and Group II containing hydraulic performance definitions.
  • Aim: Correctly match the canal outlet types to their definitions.

3. Core Concepts:

A canal outlet (or module) is a small structure built at the head of the watercourse to connect it with a minor or distributary channel. They are classified based on hydraulic behavior:

  • Non-modular outlets: Discharge depends heavily on the difference in water levels between the supply canal and the receiving watercourse.
  • Semi-modular (Flexible) outlets: Discharge depends only on the water level in the supply canal. The receiving watercourse level does not affect discharge (as long as the minimum working head is maintained).
  • Modular (Rigid) outlets: Discharge remains strictly constant, completely independent of fluctuations in the water levels of both the supply canal and the receiving watercourse (within designed limits).

4. Solution Method:

Map the definitions directly based on the core theoretical concepts above.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • P. Non-modular outlet \(\implies\) Depends on both supply and receiving water levels \(\implies\) Matches with 1
  • Q. Semi-modular outlet \(\implies\) Depends only on the supply canal water level \(\implies\) Matches with 3
  • R. Modular outlet \(\implies\) Fixed discharge, independent of both water levels \(\implies\) Matches with 2

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P — 1; Q — 3; R — 2  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A 1 m wide rectangular channel has a bed slope of 0.0016 and the Manning’s roughness coefficient is 0.04. Uniform flow takes place in the channel at a flow depth of 0.5 m. At a particular section, gradually varied flow (GVF) is observed and the flow depth is measured as 0.6 m. The GVF profile at that section is classified as
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (GVF)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Channel width \(B = 1\text{ m}\) (Rectangular)
    • Bed slope \(S_0 = 0.0016\)
    • Manning's roughness coefficient \(n = 0.04\)
    • Normal depth \(y_n = 0.5\text{ m}\)
    • Observed GVF flow depth \(y = 0.6\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Classify the Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) profile.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Manning's Equation for Uniform Flow: \(Q = \dfrac{1}{n} A R^{2/3} S_0^{1/2}\)
  • Critical Depth for Rectangular Channel: \(y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}\)
  • Slope Classification:
    • Mild (M): \(y_n > y_c\)
    • Steep (S): \(y_c > y_n\)
  • Zone Classification:
    • Zone 1: Actual depth \(y > y_n\) and \(y > y_c\)
    • Zone 2: Actual depth \(y\) is between \(y_n\) and \(y_c\)
    • Zone 3: Actual depth \(y < y_n\) and \(y < y_c\)

4. Solution Method:

  • Use normal depth and Manning's formula to calculate uniform discharge \(Q\) and unit discharge \(q\).
  • Calculate critical depth \(y_c\) using the computed \(q\).
  • Compare \(y_n\) and \(y_c\) to determine slope class (M or S).
  • Compare actual depth \(y\) with \(y_n\) and \(y_c\) to locate the zone (1, 2, or 3).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Channel properties at normal depth (\(y_n = 0.5\text{ m}\)):
    \[A = B \times y_n = 1 \times 0.5 = 0.5\text{ m}^2 \]\[P = B + 2y_n = 1 + 1 = 2.0\text{ m} \]\[R = \dfrac{A}{P} = \dfrac{0.5}{2.0} = 0.25\text{ m} \]
  2. Calculate uniform discharge \(Q\) and unit discharge \(q\):
    \[Q = \dfrac{1}{0.04} \times 0.5 \times (0.25)^{2/3} \times (0.0016)^{1/2} \]\[Q = 25 \times 0.5 \times 0.39685 \times 0.04 \approx 0.1984\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]\[q = \dfrac{Q}{B} = 0.1984\text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]
  3. Calculate Critical Depth (\(y_c\)):
    \[y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\dfrac{0.1984^2}{9.81}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\dfrac{0.03936}{9.81}\right)^{1/3} \approx 0.1589\text{ m} \]
  4. Determine Slope and Zone:
    • \(y_n (0.5\text{ m}) > y_c (0.1589\text{ m})\) \(\implies\) Mild slope (M)
    • \(y (0.6\text{ m}) > y_n (0.5\text{ m}) > y_c (0.1589\text{ m})\) \(\implies\) Actual depth lies above both normal and critical depths \(\implies\) Zone 1
    Therefore, the profile is classified as \(M_1\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Profile is classified as \(M_1\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A sluice gate used to control the flow in a horizontal channel of unit width is shown in the figure.

It is observed that the depth of flow is 1.0 m upstream of the gate, while the depth is 0.2 m downstream of the gate. Assuming a smooth flow transition across the sluice gate, i.e., without any energy loss, and the acceleration due to gravity as 10 m/s², the discharge (in m³/s, up to two decimal places) passing under the sluice gate is _______________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (Specific Energy)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Upstream flow depth: \(d_1 = 1.0\text{ m}\)
    • Downstream flow depth: \(d_2 = 0.2\text{ m}\)
    • Channel unit width: \(B = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Energy loss through gate: \(h_L = 0\) (smooth transition)
    • \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Determine the volumetric discharge \(Q\) (in m³/s) passing under the sluice gate.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Specific Energy (\(E\)): Since the channel bed is horizontal, specific energy is conserved across the gate (\(E_1 = E_2\)).
    \[E = d + \dfrac{V^2}{2g} = d + \dfrac{q^2}{2gd^2} \]where \(q\) is the discharge per unit width.
  • Continuity: For a rectangular channel of constant width, \(q = V_1 d_1 = V_2 d_2\).

4. Solution Method:

Equate specific energy at sections 1 and 2, substitute the velocity term using continuity in terms of \(q\), and solve for \(q\) and hence \(Q\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up specific energy balance:
    \[d_1 + \dfrac{q^2}{2g d_1^2} = d_2 + \dfrac{q^2}{2g d_2^2} \]
  2. Substitute values:
    \[1.0 + \dfrac{q^2}{20 \times 1^2} = 0.2 + \dfrac{q^2}{20 \times (0.2)^2} \]\[1.0 + \dfrac{q^2}{20} = 0.2 + \dfrac{q^2}{0.8} \]
  3. Solve algebraically for \(q\):
    \[1.0 - 0.2 = q^2\left(\dfrac{1}{0.8} - \dfrac{1}{20}\right) \]\[0.8 = q^2(1.25 - 0.05) = 1.2\, q^2 \]\[q^2 = \dfrac{0.8}{1.2} = \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.6667\text{ m}^4/\text{s}^2 \]\[q = \sqrt{0.6667} \approx 0.8165\text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]
  4. Total discharge:
    \[Q = q \times B = 0.8165 \times 1 \approx 0.82\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
    Sanity Check: \(Fr_1 = 0.8165/\sqrt{10 \times 1} = 0.26\) (subcritical upstream ✓); \(Fr_2 = (0.8165/0.2)/\sqrt{10 \times 0.2} = 2.88\) (supercritical downstream ✓).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.82 m³/s  |  Accepted key range: 0.80 to 0.83

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Water flows through a 90° bend in a horizontal plane as depicted in the figure.

A pressure of 140 kPa is measured at Section 1-1. The inlet diameter marked at Section 1-1 is \(\dfrac{27}{\sqrt{\pi}}\) cm, while the nozzle diameter marked at Section 2-2 is \(\dfrac{14}{\sqrt{\pi}}\) cm. Assume the following:
(i) Acceleration due to gravity = 10 m/s².
(ii) Weights of both the bent pipe segment as well as water are negligible.
(iii) Friction across the bend is negligible.
The magnitude of the force (in kN, up to two decimal places) that would be required to hold the pipe section is _______________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Fluid Dynamics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Bend angle: \(90^\circ\) in a horizontal plane
    • Inlet pressure: \(P_1 = 140\text{ kPa}\) (gauge)
    • Outlet pressure: \(P_2 = 0\text{ kPa}\) (gauge, atmospheric)
    • Inlet diameter: \(D_1 = \dfrac{0.27}{\sqrt{\pi}}\text{ m}\)
    • Outlet diameter: \(D_2 = \dfrac{0.14}{\sqrt{\pi}}\text{ m}\)
    • \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\), \(\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the magnitude of the external force (in kN) required to hold the pipe in place.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Continuity Equation: \(A_1 V_1 = A_2 V_2 = Q\)
  • Bernoulli's Equation (horizontal, frictionless):
    \[\dfrac{P_1}{\rho g} + \dfrac{V_1^2}{2g} = \dfrac{P_2}{\rho g} + \dfrac{V_2^2}{2g} \]
  • Linear Momentum Equation:
    \[\sum \vec{F} = \rho Q (\vec{V}_2 - \vec{V}_1) \]where \(\sum\vec{F}\) includes pressure forces and external holding forces on the control volume.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute areas \(A_1\) and \(A_2\); find velocity relation from continuity.
  2. Substitute into Bernoulli's equation to solve for \(V_1\) and \(V_2\).
  3. Calculate mass flow rate \(\dot{m}\).
  4. Apply momentum equation in X and Y directions to find \(F_{hold,X}\) and \(F_{hold,Y}\).
  5. Compute resultant: \(F = \sqrt{F_X^2 + F_Y^2}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Areas and velocity relation:
    \[A_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(\dfrac{0.27}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{0.27^2}{4} = 0.018225\text{ m}^2 \]\[A_2 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(\dfrac{0.14}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{0.14^2}{4} = 0.0049\text{ m}^2 \]\[V_2 = \dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\,V_1 = \dfrac{0.018225}{0.0049}\,V_1 \approx 3.7194\,V_1 \]
  2. Bernoulli's equation:
    \[14 + \dfrac{V_1^2}{20} = \dfrac{(3.7194\,V_1)^2}{20} \]\[280 + V_1^2 = 13.8338\,V_1^2 \implies V_1^2 = 21.817 \implies V_1 = 4.671\text{ m/s} \]\[V_2 = 3.7194 \times 4.671 = 17.373\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Discharge and mass flow rate:
    \[Q = A_1 V_1 = 0.018225 \times 4.671 = 0.08513\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]\[\dot{m} = 1000 \times 0.08513 = 85.13\text{ kg/s} \]
  4. Momentum equation (inlet along \(+\hat{j}\), outlet along \(+\hat{i}\)):
    X-direction:\[F_X = \dot{m}V_2 = 85.13 \times 17.373 = 1478.96\text{ N} = 1.479\text{ kN} \]Y-direction:\[F_Y + P_1 A_1 = -\dot{m}V_1 \]\[F_Y + (140{,}000 \times 0.018225) = -(85.13 \times 4.671) \]\[F_Y + 2551.5 = -397.6 \implies F_Y = -2949.1\text{ N} = -2.949\text{ kN} \]
  5. Resultant force:
    \[|\vec{F}_{hold}| = \sqrt{1.479^2 + (-2.949)^2} = \sqrt{2.187 + 8.697} = 3.30\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.30 kN  |  Accepted key range: 2.50 to 3.75

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: An effective rainfall of 2-hour duration produced a flood hydrograph peak of 200 m³/s. The flood hydrograph has a base flow of 20 m³/s. If the spatial average rainfall in the watershed for the duration of storm is 2 cm and the average loss rate is 0.4 cm/hour, the peak of 2-hour unit hydrograph (in m³/s-cm, up to one decimal place) is _______________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Unit Hydrograph

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Storm duration: \(t_r = 2\text{ hours}\)
    • Flood hydrograph peak: \(200\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Base flow: \(20\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\) (constant)
    • Total precipitation: \(P = 2\text{ cm}\)
    • Average loss rate (\(\phi\)-index): \(0.4\text{ cm/hr}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the peak of the 2-hour unit hydrograph (in m³/s-cm).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Direct Runoff Hydrograph (DRH):
    \[\text{DRH Ordinate} = \text{Flood Hydrograph Ordinate} - \text{Base Flow} \]
  • Effective Rainfall (\(R\)):
    \[R = P - \text{Total Losses} \]
  • Unit Hydrograph Proportionality:
    \[\text{Peak of UH} = \dfrac{\text{Peak of DRH}}{R} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Isolate the DRH peak by subtracting base flow from total flood peak.
  2. Calculate total rainfall loss over storm duration.
  3. Calculate effective rainfall depth \(R\).
  4. Divide DRH peak by \(R\) for UH peak.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Peak of DRH:
    \[Q_{p,DRH} = 200 - 20 = 180\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  2. Total losses:
    \[\text{Total Loss} = 0.4\text{ cm/hr} \times 2\text{ hr} = 0.8\text{ cm} \]
  3. Effective rainfall:
    \[R = 2.0 - 0.8 = 1.2\text{ cm} \]
  4. Peak of unit hydrograph:
    \[U_p = \dfrac{180}{1.2} = 150\text{ m}^3/\text{s-cm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 150.0 m³/s-cm  |  Accepted key range: 149.0 to 151.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: If a centrifugal pump has an impeller speed of \( N \) (in rpm), discharge \( Q \) (in m\(^3\)/s) and the total head \( H \) (in m), the expression for the specific speed \( N_s \) of the pump is given by
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydraulic Machines (Pumps)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: \(N\) = Impeller speed (rpm), \(Q\) = Discharge (m³/s), \(H\) = Total head (m).
  • Aim: Identify the standard equation for specific speed (\(N_s\)) of a centrifugal pump.

3. Core Concepts:

Specific speed is an index number used to classify pump impellers based on geometric similarity and performance. It denotes the speed of a geometrically similar pump delivering 1 m³/s against a 1 m head. Using Buckingham's \(\pi\)-theorem:\[N_s = \dfrac{N\sqrt{Q}}{H^{3/4}} \]

4. Solution Method:

Convert the square root and fractional exponents to decimal form: \(\sqrt{Q} = Q^{0.5}\), \(H^{3/4} = H^{0.75}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

\[N_s = \dfrac{N\,Q^{0.5}}{H^{0.75}} \]

Note: Do not confuse with specific speed of a turbine, which uses Power (\(P\)) instead of Discharge (\(Q\)): \(N_s = \dfrac{N\sqrt{P}}{H^{5/4}}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{N\,Q^{0.5}}{H^{0.75}}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: During a storm event in a certain period, the rainfall intensity is 3.5 cm/hour and the \( \Phi \)-index is 1.5 cm/hour. The intensity of effective rainfall (in cm/hour, up to one decimal place) for this period is ___________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Precipitation and Abstractions

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Rainfall intensity: \(i = 3.5 \text{ cm/hour}\)
    • \(\Phi\)-index: \(\Phi = 1.5 \text{ cm/hour}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the intensity of effective rainfall in cm/hour.

3. Core Concepts:

\(\Phi\)-index: Represents the average rainfall intensity above which rainfall equals total runoff. It acts as a constant infiltration rate limit during a continuous storm.

Effective Rainfall: The rainfall that contributes entirely to direct surface runoff:\[i_{\text{eff}} = i - \Phi \quad \text{(valid when } i > \Phi\text{, otherwise } i_{\text{eff}} = 0\text{)} \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Check: \(i = 3.5 \text{ cm/hr} > \Phi = 1.5 \text{ cm/hr}\) → surface runoff occurs.
  2. \[i_{\text{eff}} = 3.5 - 1.5 = 2.0 \text{ cm/hour} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.0 cm/hour | Accepted key range: 1.9 to 2.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q24
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The infiltration capacity of a soil follows the Horton's exponential model, \( f = c_1 + c_2 e^{-kt} \). During an experiment, the initial infiltration capacity was observed to be 200 mm/h. After a long time, the infiltration capacity was reduced to 25 mm/h. If the infiltration capacity after 1 hour was 90 mm/h, the value of the decay rate constant, \( k \) (in h\(^{-1}\), up to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Infiltration

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • General Horton's model: \(f = c_1 + c_2 e^{-kt}\)
    • Initial infiltration capacity: \(f_0 = 200 \text{ mm/h}\) (at \(t = 0\))
    • Ultimate infiltration capacity: \(f_c = 25 \text{ mm/h}\) (at \(t \to \infty\))
    • Infiltration at \(t = 1\text{ hour}\): \(f_1 = 90 \text{ mm/h}\)
  • Aim: Find the decay rate constant \(k\) (in h\(^{-1}\)) to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Horton's Infiltration Equation:\[f_t = f_c + (f_0 - f_c)\,e^{-kt} \]where \(f_0\) = initial capacity, \(f_c\) = ultimate capacity, \(k\) = decay constant.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Map model constants to physical parameters: \(c_1 = f_c\), \(c_2 = f_0 - f_c\).
  2. Substitute known values and solve for \(e^{-k}\).
  3. Take natural logarithm to isolate \(k\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(c_1 = 25 \text{ mm/h}\),   \(c_2 = 200 - 25 = 175 \text{ mm/h}\)
  2. Substitute at \(t = 1\text{ h}\), \(f_t = 90 \text{ mm/h}\):\[90 = 25 + 175\,e^{-k} \implies 65 = 175\,e^{-k} \implies e^{-k} = \dfrac{65}{175} \approx 0.3714 \]
  3. Take natural logarithm:\[-k = \ln(0.3714) \approx -0.9904 \implies k \approx 0.99 \text{ h}^{-1} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.99 h\(^{-1}\) | Accepted key range: 0.98 to 1.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
The figure shows a U-tube having a 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section filled with mercury (specific gravity = 13.6) up to a height of 20 cm in each limb (open to the atmosphere).


If 5 cm³ of water is added to the right limb, the new height (in cm, up to two decimal places) of mercury in the LEFT limb will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Fluid Statics / Manometry

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • U-tube with square cross-section: \(5 \text{ mm} \times 5 \text{ mm}\)
    • Initial fluid: Mercury (\(S_{Hg} = 13.6\)), filled to 20 cm in each limb
    • Added fluid: Water (\(V_w = 5 \text{ cm}^3\)) added to the right limb
  • Aim: Determine the new height of mercury in the left limb (in cm, to 2 decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

Hydrostatic Law: \(\Delta P = \gamma h\)    Pascal's Principle: Pressure equilibrium at any horizontal datum in a connected fluid.

Manometric Equation: Equate hydrostatic pressure on both sides at the lowest mercury interface datum.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert cross-sectional area to cm² and compute height of water column.
  2. Let mercury fall by \(x\) cm in the right limb → rises by \(x\) cm in the left limb.
  3. Equate gauge pressure heads at the mercury-water interface datum.
  4. Solve for \(x\); add to initial left-limb height.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Area and Water Column Height:
    \(A = 5 \text{ mm} \times 5 \text{ mm} = 25 \text{ mm}^2 = 0.25 \text{ cm}^2\)\[h_w = \dfrac{V_w}{A} = \dfrac{5 \text{ cm}^3}{0.25 \text{ cm}^2} = 20 \text{ cm} \]
  2. Equilibrium State:
    Mercury falls \(x\) cm in right limb → rises \(x\) cm in left limb.
    Net difference in mercury levels: \(h_{Hg} = 2x\) cm.
  3. Pressure Equilibrium at the Interface Datum:\[S_{Hg} \times 2x = S_w \times h_w \]\[13.6 \times 2x = 1 \times 20 \implies 27.2x = 20 \implies x = \dfrac{20}{27.2} \approx 0.7353 \text{ cm} \]
  4. New Height in Left Limb:\[h_{\text{left}} = 20 + x = 20 + 0.7353 = 20.74 \text{ cm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 20.74 cm | Accepted key range: 20.70 to 20.76

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A 1 m wide rectangular channel carries a discharge of 2 m³/s. The specific energy-depth diagram is prepared for the channel. It is observed in this diagram that corresponding to a particular specific energy, the subcritical depth is twice the supercritical depth. The subcritical depth (in meters, up to two decimal places) is equal to ___________
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Specific Energy

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Channel shape: Rectangular, width \(b = 1 \text{ m}\)
    • Discharge: \(Q = 2 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Alternate depths: Subcritical depth \(y_2 = 2y_1\) (supercritical depth)
  • Aim: Find the subcritical depth \(y_2\) in meters (to 2 decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

Specific Energy:\[E = y + \dfrac{q^2}{2gy^2} \]

Alternate Depths: Two depths (\(y_1, y_2\)) passing the same \(q\) at the same specific energy \(E\).

Unit discharge: \(q = Q/b\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute unit discharge \(q\).
  2. Equate specific energy at both alternate depths: \(E_1 = E_2\).
  3. Substitute \(y_2 = 2y_1\) and solve for \(y_1\).
  4. Compute \(y_2 = 2y_1\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Unit Discharge: \(q = 2/1 = 2 \text{ m}^2/\text{s}\)
  2. Equate Specific Energy (substituting \(y_2 = 2y_1\)):\[y_1 + \dfrac{q^2}{2gy_1^2} = 2y_1 + \dfrac{q^2}{2g(2y_1)^2} \]\[y_1 + \dfrac{q^2}{2gy_1^2} = 2y_1 + \dfrac{q^2}{8gy_1^2} \]
  3. Rearrange and Solve for \(y_1\):\[2y_1 - y_1 = \dfrac{q^2}{2gy_1^2} - \dfrac{q^2}{8gy_1^2} = \dfrac{q^2}{gy_1^2} \cdot \dfrac{3}{8} \]\[y_1^3 = \dfrac{3q^2}{8g} = \dfrac{3 \times 4}{8 \times 9.81} = \dfrac{12}{78.48} \approx 0.15291 \]\[y_1 = (0.15291)^{1/3} \approx 0.5347 \text{ m} \]
  4. Subcritical Depth:\[y_2 = 2 \times 0.5347 = 1.07 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.07 m | Accepted key range: 1.06 to 1.08

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A catchment is idealized as a 25 km × 25 km square. It has five rain gauges, one at each corner and one at the center, as shown in the figure.


During a month, the precipitation at these gauges is measured as G₁ = 300 mm, G₂ = 285 mm, G₃ = 272 mm, G₄ = 290 mm and G₅ = 288 mm. The average precipitation (in mm, up to one decimal place) over the catchment during this month by using the Thiessen polygon method is ___________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Precipitation Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Catchment: Square, \(25 \text{ km} \times 25 \text{ km}\)
    • Rain gauges: 4 at corners (\(G_1, G_2, G_3, G_4\)) and 1 at center (\(G_5\))
    • Recorded precipitation: \(G_1 = 300\), \(G_2 = 285\), \(G_3 = 272\), \(G_4 = 290\), \(G_5 = 288\) (all in mm)
  • Aim: Evaluate the mean areal precipitation using the Thiessen polygon method.

3. Core Concepts:

Thiessen Polygon Method: Defines boundaries using perpendicular bisectors between adjacent gauges, allocating areal weights proportional to regions closest to each gauge.

\[P_{avg} = \sum (P_i W_i) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine geometric polygons from perpendicular bisectors.
  2. Extract proportional area weights (\(W_i\)) relative to total area.
  3. Apply weights to point rainfall depths.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Geometrical Construction:
    The perpendicular bisectors between the center gauge (\(G_5\)) and each corner gauge form an inner tilted square. Its vertices fall on the midpoints of the outer boundary. Area of central polygon:\[A_5 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times L \times L = 0.5L^2 \]
  2. Area Weights:
    GaugeAreaWeight (\(W_i\))
    \(G_5\) (center)\(0.5L^2\)0.50
    \(G_1, G_2, G_3, G_4\) (corners)\(0.125L^2\) each0.125 each
  3. Mean Precipitation:\[P_{avg} = 0.125 \times (300 + 285 + 272 + 290) + 0.50 \times 288 \]\[P_{avg} = 0.125 \times 1147 + 144 = 143.375 + 144 = 287.375 \approx 287.4 \text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 287.4 mm | Accepted key range: 286.9 to 287.9

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The culturable command area of a canal is 10,000 ha. The area grows only two crops—rice in the Kharif season and wheat in the Rabi season. The design discharge of the canal is based on the rice requirements, which has an irrigated area of 2500 ha, base period of 150 days and delta of 130 cm. The maximum permissible irrigated area (in ha) for wheat, with a base period of 120 days and delta of 50 cm, is ___________
questions.explanation:
Irrigation Engineering | Water Requirements of Crops

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Culturable Command Area (CCA) = 10,000 ha
    • Rice irrigated area: \(A_r = 2500 \text{ ha}\), Base period: \(B_r = 150 \text{ days}\), Delta: \(\Delta_r = 130 \text{ cm} = 1.30 \text{ m}\)
    • Wheat Base period: \(B_w = 120 \text{ days}\), Delta: \(\Delta_w = 50 \text{ cm} = 0.50 \text{ m}\)
    • Design discharge of the canal is fixed by Rice requirements.
  • Aim: Find the maximum permissible irrigated area for wheat (\(A_w\)) in hectares.

3. Core Concepts:

Duty (\(D\)): The area of land (in hectares) irrigated by a constant discharge of \(1 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\) (cumec) flowing continuously throughout the base period:\[D = \dfrac{8.64 \times B}{\Delta} \]where \(B\) is in days, \(\Delta\) is in meters, and \(D\) is in ha/cumec.

Discharge (\(Q\)): \(Q = \dfrac{\text{Area}\,(A)}{\text{Duty}\,(D)}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the Duty of water for Rice.
  2. Determine the maximum design discharge (\(Q_{design}\)) based on Rice area.
  3. Calculate the Duty of water for Wheat.
  4. Using \(Q_{design}\), determine the maximum irrigable Wheat area and check against CCA.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Duty of Rice (\(D_r\)):\[D_r = \dfrac{8.64 \times 150}{1.30} = 996.923 \text{ ha/cumec} \]
  2. Canal Design Discharge (\(Q_{design}\)):\[Q_{design} = \dfrac{A_r}{D_r} = \dfrac{2500}{996.923} = 2.5077 \text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  3. Duty of Wheat (\(D_w\)):\[D_w = \dfrac{8.64 \times 120}{0.50} = 2073.6 \text{ ha/cumec} \]
  4. Maximum Irrigated Area for Wheat (\(A_w\)):\[A_w = Q_{design} \times D_w = 2.5077 \times 2073.6 = 5200 \text{ ha} \]Constraint check: \(5200 \text{ ha} \le 10{,}000 \text{ ha}\) (CCA). ✓ Valid.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5200 ha | Accepted key range: 5150 to 5250

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: Water is pumped at a steady uniform flow rate of 0.01 m³/s through a horizontal smooth circular pipe of 100 mm diameter. Given that the Reynolds number is 800 and g is 9.81 m/s², the head loss (in meters, up to one decimal place) per km length due to friction would be ___________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Flow Through Pipes

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Discharge: \(Q = 0.01 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Diameter: \(D = 100 \text{ mm} = 0.1 \text{ m}\)
    • Reynolds Number: \(Re = 800\) (Laminar flow since \(Re < 2000\))
    • Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.81 \text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Length: \(L = 1 \text{ km} = 1000 \text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Find the head loss per km due to friction (\(h_f\)) in meters (1 decimal place).

3. Core Concepts:

Darcy-Weisbach Equation: \(h_f = \dfrac{f \cdot L \cdot v^2}{2 \cdot g \cdot D}\)

Friction Factor for Laminar Flow: \(f = \dfrac{64}{Re}\)

Continuity Equation: \(v = \dfrac{Q}{A}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the cross-sectional area and average flow velocity (\(v\)).
  2. Evaluate the friction factor (\(f\)) using the given Reynolds Number.
  3. Apply the Darcy-Weisbach equation to find the head loss for \(L = 1000 \text{ m}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute Flow Velocity (\(v\)):\[A = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4} = \dfrac{\pi \times (0.1)^2}{4} = 0.007854 \text{ m}^2 \]\[v = \dfrac{Q}{A} = \dfrac{0.01}{0.007854} = 1.2732 \text{ m/s} \]
  2. Friction Factor (\(f\)):\[f = \dfrac{64}{Re} = \dfrac{64}{800} = 0.08 \]
  3. Head Loss (\(h_f\)):\[h_f = \dfrac{0.08 \times 1000 \times (1.2732)^2}{2 \times 9.81 \times 0.1} = \dfrac{80 \times 1.621}{1.962} = \dfrac{129.68}{1.962} = 66.1 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 66.1 m | Accepted key range: 65.0 to 69.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The direct runoff hydrograph in response to 5 cm rainfall excess in a catchment is shown in the figure. The area of the catchment (expressed in hectares) is _______________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Hydrographs — Catchment Area from DRH

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Rainfall excess: \(R = 5\text{ cm} = 0.05\text{ m}\)
    • Peak discharge: \(Q_p = 1\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Base time: \(t_b = 6\text{ hours}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the catchment area in hectares.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total runoff volume = Area under the DRH (triangular hydrograph).
  • \(\text{Volume} = A \times R\), where \(A\) = catchment area.
  • Area of triangle: \(\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Base time in seconds: \(6 \times 3600 = 21600\text{ s}\)
  2. Volume of runoff:\[V = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 21600 \times 1 = 10800\text{ m}^3 \]
  3. Catchment area:\[V = A \times R \implies 10800 = A \times 0.05 \implies A = 216000\text{ m}^2 \]
  4. Convert to hectares (\(1\text{ ha} = 10^4\text{ m}^2\)):\[A = \dfrac{216000}{10000} = 21.6\text{ ha} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 21.6 hectares | Accepted key range: [21.5, 21.7]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q15
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
The type of flood routing (Group I) and the equation(s) used for the purpose (Group II) are given below.

Group IGroup II
P   Hydrologic flood routing1.   Continuity equation
Q   Hydraulic flood routing2.   Momentum equation
3.   Energy equation

The correct match is
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Flood Routing — Governing Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Group I: Hydrologic routing (P), Hydraulic routing (Q). Group II: Continuity (1), Momentum (2), Energy (3) equations.
  • Aim: Match routing methods with their governing equations.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Hydrologic Routing (Lumped): Uses only the Continuity Equation (\(I - Q = dS/dt\)). Spatial variation of flow is ignored.
  • Hydraulic Routing (Distributed): Uses the Saint-Venant equations: both Continuity and Momentum equations, accounting for spatial and temporal variation.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • P (Hydrologic) → 1 (Continuity only)
  • Q (Hydraulic) → 1 & 2 (Continuity and Momentum)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P – 1; Q – 1 & 2 | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q16
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The pre-jump Froude Number for a particular flow in a horizontal rectangular channel is 10. The ratio of sequent depths (i.e., post-jump depth to pre-jump depth) is _______________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow — Hydraulic Jump Sequent Depths

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Channel: horizontal rectangular
    • Pre-jump Froude number: \(F_{r1} = 10\)
  • Aim: Calculate the sequent depth ratio \(y_2/y_1\).

3. Core Concepts:

Belanger Momentum Equation for hydraulic jump in a rectangular channel:\[\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8F_{r1}^2} - 1\right) \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Substitute \(F_{r1} = 10\):\[\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8(10)^2} - 1\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{801} - 1\right) \]
  2. \(\sqrt{801} \approx 28.3019\)
  3. \[\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = \dfrac{1}{2}(28.3019 - 1) = \dfrac{27.3019}{2} \approx 13.65 \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 13.65 | Accepted key range: [13.6, 13.7]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A concrete gravity dam section is shown in the figure. Assuming unit weight of water as 10 kN/m3 and unit weight of concrete as 24 kN/m3, the uplift force per unit length of the dam (expressed in kN/m) at PQ is _______________
questions.explanation:
Water Resources / Irrigation Engineering | Dams — Uplift Pressure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Upstream water depth: \(H = 65\text{ m}\)
    • Downstream water depth: \(h = 5\text{ m}\)
    • Distance from upstream face to gallery: \(L_1 = 10\text{ m}\)
    • Distance from gallery to downstream face: \(L_2 = 40\text{ m}\)
    • Total base width: \(B = 50\text{ m}\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the total uplift force per unit length of the dam (kN/m).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Hydrostatic Pressure: \(u = \gamma_w \times \text{depth}\)
  • IS 6512 — Uplift at Drainage Gallery: Uplift pressure at the drainage gallery is taken as tailwater pressure plus one-third of the headwater–tailwater pressure difference:\[u_D = u_{downstream} + \dfrac{1}{3}(u_{upstream} - u_{downstream}) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate uplift pressure at upstream heel (\(u_P\)) and downstream toe (\(u_Q\)).
  2. Calculate uplift pressure at the drainage gallery (\(u_D\)) using IS 6512.
  3. Compute total uplift force as the sum of areas of two trapezoidal blocks.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Pressures at Heel and Toe:\[u_P = 10 \times 65 = 650\text{ kPa} \]\[u_Q = 10 \times 5 = 50\text{ kPa} \]
  2. Pressure at Drainage Gallery:\[u_D = 50 + \dfrac{1}{3}(650 - 50) = 50 + 200 = 250\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Total Uplift Force per Unit Length:
    SegmentLength (m)Pressures (kPa)Force (kN/m)
    Heel P to Gallery10\(\dfrac{1}{2}(650+250)\times10\)4500
    Gallery to Toe Q40\(\dfrac{1}{2}(250+50)\times40\)6000
    Total50—10500
    \[F_U = 4500 + 6000 = 10500\text{ kN/m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10500 kN/m | Accepted key range: [10490, 10510]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A 4 m wide rectangular channel, having bed slope of 0.001 carries a discharge of 16 m3/s. Considering Manning's roughness coefficient = 0.012 and \( g = 10 \) m/s2, the category of the channel slope is
questions.explanation:
Water Resources / Fluid Mechanics & Hydraulics | Open Channel Flow — Slope Classification

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Channel type: Rectangular, width \(b = 4\text{ m}\)
    • Discharge: \(Q = 16\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Bed slope: \(S_0 = 0.001\)
    • Manning's roughness: \(n = 0.012\)
    • \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Determine whether the slope is Mild, Critical, Steep, or Horizontal.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Slope Classification:
    • Mild (M): \(y_n > y_c\) or \(S_0 < S_c\)
    • Critical (C): \(y_n = y_c\) or \(S_0 = S_c\)
    • Steep (S): \(y_n < y_c\) or \(S_0 > S_c\)
  • Critical Depth (rectangular channel): \(y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}\)
  • Manning's Equation: \(Q = \dfrac{1}{n} A R^{2/3} S^{1/2}\)

4. Solution Method:

Compute the critical slope \(S_c\) corresponding to \(y_c\) and compare with \(S_0\). This avoids trial-and-error for normal depth.

  1. Find discharge per unit width (\(q\)) and compute critical depth (\(y_c\)).
  2. Evaluate section properties at critical state: \(A_c\), \(P_c\), \(R_c\).
  3. Use Manning's equation to solve for critical slope (\(S_c\)).
  4. Compare \(S_0\) with \(S_c\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Critical Depth (\(y_c\)):\[q = \dfrac{Q}{b} = \dfrac{16}{4} = 4\text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]\[y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\dfrac{16}{10}\right)^{1/3} = (1.6)^{1/3} \approx 1.1696\text{ m} \]
  2. Section Properties at Critical State:\[A_c = b \times y_c = 4 \times 1.1696 = 4.6784\text{ m}^2 \]\[P_c = b + 2y_c = 4 + 2(1.1696) = 6.3392\text{ m} \]\[R_c = \dfrac{A_c}{P_c} = \dfrac{4.6784}{6.3392} \approx 0.7380\text{ m} \]
  3. Critical Slope (\(S_c\)):\[S_c = \left(\dfrac{n \cdot Q}{A_c \cdot R_c^{2/3}}\right)^2 \]\[R_c^{2/3} = (0.7380)^{0.6667} \approx 0.8166 \]\[S_c = \left(\dfrac{0.012 \times 16}{4.6784 \times 0.8166}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{0.192}{3.8204}\right)^2 \approx (0.05026)^2 \approx 0.002526 \]
  4. Comparison:
    \(S_0 = 0.001 < S_c = 0.002526\)
    The actual slope is gentler than the critical slope → normal depth \(y_n > y_c\) → Mild Slope.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Mild slope | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A sector gate is provided on a spillway as shown in the figure. Assuming \( g = 10 \) m/s2, the resultant force per meter length (expressed in kN/m) on the gate will be _______________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Fluid Statics — Curved Surface Hydrostatic Force

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Radius of sector gate: \(R = 5\text{ m}\)
    • Subtended angle: \(30^\circ\) above and \(30^\circ\) below horizontal (\(60^\circ\) total)
    • \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\), \(\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3 \implies \gamma = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the resultant hydrostatic force per meter length on the gate in kN/m.

3. Core Concepts:

For a curved surface, the resultant hydrostatic force has two components:

  • Horizontal Force (\(F_H\)): Equal to the hydrostatic force on the vertical projected area of the curved surface.\[F_H = \gamma\,\bar{h}\,A_{proj} \]
  • Vertical Force (\(F_V\)): Equal to the weight of liquid (real or imaginary) supported by the curved surface up to the free surface.
  • Resultant: \(F = \sqrt{F_H^2 + F_V^2}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Horizontal Force (\(F_H\)):
    Total gate height: \(h = 5\sin(30^\circ) + 5\sin(30^\circ) = 2.5 + 2.5 = 5\text{ m}\)
    Projected area per meter: \(A_{proj} = 5 \times 1 = 5\text{ m}^2\)
    Centroid depth: \(\bar{h} = 5/2 = 2.5\text{ m}\)\[F_H = 10 \times 2.5 \times 5 = 125\text{ kN/m} \]
  2. Vertical Force (\(F_V\)):
    Net vertical force = weight of water in the circular segment (closed gate profile volume).
    Area of circular sector:\[A_{sector} = \dfrac{1}{2}R^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}(25)\left(\dfrac{60\pi}{180}\right) = \dfrac{25\pi}{6} = 13.090\text{ m}^2 \]Area of triangle (hinge to gate ends): base \(= 5\text{ m}\), height \(= 5\cos(30^\circ) = 4.330\text{ m}\)\[A_{triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4.330 = 10.825\text{ m}^2 \]Area of circular segment:\[A_{seg} = 13.090 - 10.825 = 2.265\text{ m}^2 \]\[F_V = \gamma \times A_{seg} \times 1 = 10 \times 2.265 = 22.65\text{ kN/m} \]
  3. Resultant Force (\(F\)):\[F = \sqrt{125^2 + 22.65^2} = \sqrt{15625 + 513.02} = \sqrt{16138.02} \approx 127.03\text{ kN/m} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 127.03 kN/m | Accepted key range: [126.0, 128.0]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A hydraulically efficient trapezoidal channel section has a uniform flow depth of 2 m. The bed width (expressed in m) of the channel is _______________
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Uniform Flow — Most Efficient Trapezoidal Section

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall & Application
  • Given Data: Flow depth \(y = 2\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Find the bed width (\(B\)) for the most hydraulically efficient trapezoidal channel section.

3. Core Concepts:

A hydraulically efficient trapezoidal section maximises discharge for a given area (minimises wetted perimeter). Its geometric properties are:

  • It forms half of a regular hexagon.
  • Side slopes: \(m = \tan(30^\circ) = 1/\sqrt{3}\) (H:V)
  • Sloping side length equals bed width \(B\).
  • Hydraulic radius: \(R = y/2\)
  • Relationship between bed width and depth: \(B = \dfrac{2y}{\sqrt{3}}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Bed Width:\[B = \dfrac{2y}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2 \times 2}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{4}{1.73205} = 2.3094\text{ m} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.31 m | Accepted key range: [2.29, 2.32]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Profile of a weir on permeable foundation is shown in figure I and an elementary profile of 'upstream pile only case' according to Khosla's theory is shown in figure II. The uplift pressure heads at key points Q, R and S are 3.14 m, 2.75 m and 0 m, respectively (refer figure II).



What is the uplift pressure head at point P downstream of the weir (junction of floor and pile as shown in the figure I)?
questions.explanation:
Irrigation Engineering | Seepage Theory (Khosla's Theory)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Figure I (Actual Case): Weir with elementary downstream pile. Total floor length = 40 m, Pile depth = 5 m, Total upstream head \(H = 4\text{ m}\). Point P = junction of floor and downstream pile (upstream face).
    • Figure II (Reference Case): Khosla's elementary profile for upstream pile only. Floor length = 40 m, Pile depth = 5 m, Total head = 4 m. Point R = junction of pile and floor (downstream face). Head at R: \(h_R = 2.75\text{ m}\).
  • Aim: Find the uplift pressure head at point P (\(h_P\)) in Figure I.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Khosla's Method of Independent Variables: Complex weir profiles are decomposed into standard elementary profiles.
  • Principle of Reversibility: If seepage flow direction is reversed, the head loss pattern mirrors itself exactly:\[\phi_{E(\text{Downstream Pile})} = 100\% - \phi_{C_1(\text{Upstream Pile})} \]

4. Solution Method:

Relate the actual downstream pile (Fig I) to the standard upstream pile (Fig II) using Khosla's Reversibility Principle.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify Homologous Points:
    • Point R in Fig II = downstream face of upstream pile (Point \(C_1\)).
    • Point P in Fig I = upstream face of downstream pile (Point \(E\)).
    • By reversibility symmetry: \(\phi_P + \phi_R = 100\%\)
  2. Convert to absolute pressure heads:\[h_P + h_R = H \]
  3. Calculate uplift head at P:\[h_P = H - h_R = 4 - 2.75 = 1.25\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.25 m | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q15
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: Water table of an aquifer drops by 100 cm over an area of 1000 km². The porosity and specific retention of the aquifer material are 25% and 5%, respectively. The amount of water (expressed in km³) drained out from the area is _________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology & Groundwater | Aquifer Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Catchment area \(A = 1000\text{ km}^2\)
    • Drop in water table \(\Delta h = 100\text{ cm} = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Porosity \(n = 0.25\)
    • Specific retention \(S_r = 0.05\)
  • Aim: Calculate the volume of water drained out of the aquifer in km³.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Specific Yield (\(S_y\)): The ratio of volume of water that freely drains under gravity to total volume of soil.\[n = S_y + S_r \]
  • Volume of water drained: \(V_w = S_y \times V_{\text{total}}\)

4. Solution Method:

Determine specific yield from porosity and specific retention. Multiply by the total unwatered aquifer volume.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Specific Yield (\(S_y\)):\[S_y = n - S_r = 0.25 - 0.05 = 0.20 \]
  2. Convert dimensions to km:
    \(A = 1000\text{ km}^2\),   \(\Delta h = 1\text{ m} = 10^{-3}\text{ km}\)
  3. Total unwatered volume:\[V_{\text{total}} = 1000 \times 10^{-3} = 1\text{ km}^3 \]
  4. Volume of water drained:\[V_w = 0.20 \times 1 = 0.20\text{ km}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.20 km³ | Accepted key range: 0.19 to 0.21

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q16
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Group I contains the types of fluids while Group II contains the shear stress - rate of shear relationship of different types of fluids, as shown in the figure.

Group I    Group II
P. Newtonian fluid1. Curve 1
Q. Pseudo plastic fluid2. Curve 2
R. Plastic fluid3. Curve 3
S. Dilatant fluid4. Curve 4
5. Curve 5



The correct match between Group I and Group II is
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Properties of Fluids

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A graph showing shear stress (\(\tau\)) vs. rate of shear (\(\dfrac{du}{dy}\)) for 5 different fluid types.
  • Aim: Match fluid types in Group I with their corresponding curves in Group II.

3. Core Concepts:

Newton's Law of Viscosity: \(\tau = \mu \dfrac{du}{dy}\). For non-Newtonian fluids, the general Power Law (Ostwald-de Waele) is:

\[\tau = A\left(\dfrac{du}{dy}\right)^n + B \]
Fluid TypeParametersCurve BehaviorCurve
Ideal Fluid\(\tau = 0\) alwaysAlong the x-axis1
Newtonian Fluid\(n=1,\; B=0\)Straight line through origin2
Dilatant (Shear Thickening)\(n>1,\; B=0\)Concave upward from origin3
Pseudo-plastic (Shear Thinning)\(n<1,\; B=0\)Concave downward from origin4
Bingham Plastic\(n=1,\; B>0\)Starts from positive y-intercept (yield stress)5

4. Solution Method & Execution:

  • P. Newtonian fluid → straight line from origin → Curve 2
  • Q. Pseudo-plastic fluid → concave downward from origin → Curve 4
  • R. Plastic fluid → starts with yield stress on y-axis → Curve 5
  • S. Dilatant fluid → concave upward from origin → Curve 3

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P-2, Q-4, R-5, S-3 | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A square plate is suspended vertically from one of its edges using a hinge support as shown in figure. A water jet of 20 mm diameter having a velocity of 10 m/s strikes the plate at its mid-point, at an angle of 30° with the vertical. Consider g as 9.81 m/s² and neglect the self-weight of the plate. The force F (expressed in N) required to keep the plate in its vertical position is _________.
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Fluid Dynamics (Impact of Jets)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Jet diameter \(d = 20\text{ mm} = 0.02\text{ m}\)
    • Jet velocity \(v = 10\text{ m/s}\)
    • Angle of jet with the vertical plate \(\alpha = 30^\circ\)
    • Lever arm for Jet Force (\(F_n\)) from hinge: \(y_1 = 200\text{ mm} = 0.2\text{ m}\)
    • Lever arm for Balancing Force (\(F\)) from hinge: \(y_2 = 400\text{ mm} = 0.4\text{ m}\)
    • Density of water \(\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the horizontal force \(F\) applied at the bottom edge to maintain the plate's vertical state.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Impulse-Momentum Principle: The normal force exerted by a jet striking a flat stationary plate at an angle \(\theta\) with the plate is:\[F_n = \rho A v^2 \sin\theta \]
  • Static Rotational Equilibrium: \(\sum M_{\text{hinge}} = 0\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the cross-sectional area of the jet.
  2. Determine the force \(F_n\) acting perpendicular to the plate (acts purely horizontally since the plate is vertical).
  3. Equate the clockwise moment caused by the jet force to the counter-clockwise moment caused by the stabilizing force \(F\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Normal Force from Jet (\(F_n\)):
    Jet Area: \(A = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.02)^2 = 3.1416 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2\)\[F_n = 1000 \times (3.1416 \times 10^{-4}) \times (10)^2 \times \sin(30^\circ) \]\[F_n = 1000 \times 0.00031416 \times 100 \times 0.5 = 15.708\text{ N} \]
  2. Moment Equilibrium About the Hinge:\[F_n \times 0.2 = F \times 0.4 \]\[F = 15.708 \times \dfrac{0.2}{0.4} = 7.854\text{ N} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 7.85 N | Accepted key range: 7.4 to 8.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The ordinates of a one-hour unit hydrograph at sixty minute interval are 0, 3, 12, 8, 6, 3 and 0 m³/s. A two-hour storm of 4 cm excess rainfall occurred in the basin from 10 AM. Considering constant base flow of 20 m³/s, the flow of the river (expressed in m³/s) at 1 PM is _________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Unit Hydrograph

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • 1-hour Unit Hydrograph (1-h UH) ordinates at 1-hour intervals: 0, 3, 12, 8, 6, 3, 0 m³/s
    • Duration of storm \(D = 2\text{ hours}\)
    • Total excess rainfall \(R = 4\text{ cm}\) over 2 hours
    • Storm starting time: 10 AM
    • Base flow \(= 20\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
  • Aim: Determine the total flow of the river at 1 PM (i.e., exactly 3 hours after the storm begins).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Superposition Principle (Linearity): A 2-hour storm producing 4 cm total excess rainfall is analyzed as two consecutive 1-hour storms.
    Intensity = 4 cm / 2 hrs = 2 cm/hr.
    Pulse 1: 2 cm excess rainfall in the 1st hour.
    Pulse 2: 2 cm excess rainfall in the 2nd hour (lagged by 1 hour).
  • Total Flow Calculation: Total River Flow = Direct Runoff Hydrograph (DRH) + Base Flow

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the relevant time ordinate: 10 AM to 1 PM → \(t = 3\text{ hours}\).
  2. Extract the 1-h UH ordinates at \(t = 3\) (for Pulse 1) and \(t = 2\) (for Pulse 2, lagged by 1 hour).
  3. Multiply by the pulse excess rainfall (2 cm) and sum to get the DRH at 1 PM.
  4. Add constant base flow to find total river flow.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Relevant Unit Hydrograph Ordinates:
    At \(t = 2\text{ h}\): \(U(2) = 12\text{ m}^3/\text{s/cm}\)
    At \(t = 3\text{ h}\): \(U(3) = 8\text{ m}^3/\text{s/cm}\)
  2. DRH at \(t = 3\text{ hours}\):\[ Q_d(3) = [2 \times U(3)] + [2 \times U(2)] = (2 \times 8) + (2 \times 12) = 16 + 24 = 40\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  3. Total River Flow:\[\text{Total Flow} = 40 + 20 = 60\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]

Self-Check (S-Curve Method): 2-h UH ordinate at \(t=3\) is \((23-3)/2 = 10\text{ m}^3/\text{s/cm}\). Multiply by 4 cm: \(10 \times 4 = 40\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\). Adding base flow: \(40 + 20 = 60\). ✓ Confirmed.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 60 m³/s | Accepted key range: 59 to 61

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A 3 m wide rectangular channel carries a flow of 6 m³/s. The depth of flow at a section P is 0.5 m. A flat-topped hump is to be placed at the downstream of the section P. Assume negligible energy loss between section P and hump, and consider g as 9.81 m/s². The maximum height of the hump (expressed in m) which will not change the depth of flow at section P is _________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Width of rectangular channel: \(B = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Discharge: \(Q = 6\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Depth at section P: \(y_1 = 0.5\text{ m}\)
    • \(g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Negligible energy loss between section P and the hump.
  • Aim: Find the maximum height of the hump (\(\Delta z\)) that will not alter the upstream depth of flow at section P.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Specific Energy (\(E\)): \(E = y + \dfrac{V^2}{2g}\)
  • Critical Flow Condition: Placing a hump decreases specific energy of flow by \(\Delta z\). Upstream conditions remain unaltered until the flow over the hump becomes critical (choking limit).
  • Critical Depth and Minimum Specific Energy for a rectangular channel:\[y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}, \qquad E_c = \dfrac{3}{2}y_c \]where \(q\) is the discharge per unit width.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine discharge per unit width (\(q\)) and specific energy at section P (\(E_1\)).
  2. Check if upstream flow is subcritical or supercritical by comparing \(y_1\) with \(y_c\).
  3. Under the limiting condition, flow over the hump becomes critical → specific energy over hump equals \(E_c\).
  4. Apply energy equation: \(E_1 = E_c + \Delta z_{\max}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Discharge per unit width (\(q\)):\[q = \dfrac{Q}{B} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2\text{ m}^3/\text{s/m} \]
  2. Velocity and Specific Energy at section P:\[V_1 = \dfrac{q}{y_1} = \dfrac{2}{0.5} = 4\text{ m/s} \]\[E_1 = 0.5 + \dfrac{4^2}{2 \times 9.81} = 0.5 + 0.8155 = 1.3155\text{ m} \]
  3. Critical Depth (\(y_c\)) and Critical Energy (\(E_c\)):\[y_c = \left(\dfrac{4}{9.81}\right)^{1/3} = (0.4077)^{1/3} = 0.7415\text{ m} \]Since \(y_1 = 0.5\text{ m} < y_c = 0.7415\text{ m}\), the incoming flow is supercritical.\[E_c = 1.5 \times 0.7415 = 1.1123\text{ m} \]
  4. Maximum Hump Height (\(\Delta z_{\max}\)):\[\Delta z_{\max} = E_1 - E_c = 1.3155 - 1.1123 = 0.2032\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.203 m | Accepted key range: 0.19 to 0.21

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A penstock of 1 m diameter and 5 km length is used to supply water from a reservoir to an impulse turbine. A nozzle of 15 cm diameter is fixed at the end of the penstock. The elevation difference between the turbine and water level in the reservoir is 500 m. Consider the head loss due to friction as 5% of the velocity head available at the jet. Assume unit weight of water = 10 kN/m³ and acceleration due to gravity (g) = 10 m/s². If the overall efficiency is 80%, power generated (expressed in kW and rounded to nearest integer) is _________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydraulic Machines

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Penstock: \(D = 1\text{ m}\), \(L = 5000\text{ m}\)
    • Nozzle diameter: \(d = 0.15\text{ m}\)
    • Gross Head: \(H = 500\text{ m}\)
    • Head loss due to friction: \(h_f = 5\%\) of the velocity head at the jet
    • Specific weight of water: \(\gamma = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Overall efficiency: \(\eta_o = 0.80\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total power generated by the turbine in kW.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Bernoulli's Energy Equation: Gross head drives flow and is converted into velocity head at the jet, minus frictional losses.
  • Power Output of Turbine:\[P = \eta_o \cdot \gamma \cdot Q \cdot H_{\text{net}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Formulate the head loss equation: \(H = H_{\text{net}} + h_f\).
  2. Substitute \(h_f = 0.05\,H_{\text{net}}\) to find jet velocity (\(v\)).
  3. Use continuity equation at the nozzle to find flow rate (\(Q\)).
  4. Compute power using overall efficiency.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Energy Equation:\[500 = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} + 0.05\dfrac{v^2}{2g} = 1.05\left(\dfrac{v^2}{2g}\right) \]
  2. Jet Velocity (\(v\)) and Effective Head (\(H_{\text{net}}\)):\[H_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} = \dfrac{500}{1.05} = 476.19\text{ m} \]\[v = \sqrt{476.19 \times 20} = \sqrt{9523.8} = 97.59\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Discharge (\(Q\)):\[Q = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.15)^2 \times 97.59 = 0.01767 \times 97.59 = 1.7246\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  4. Generated Power (\(P\)):\[P = 0.80 \times 10\text{ kN/m}^3 \times 1.7246\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \times 476.19\text{ m} = 6570\text{ kW} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6570 kW | Accepted key range: 6560 to 6580

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: In a two-dimensional steady flow field, in a certain region of the x-y plane, the velocity component in the x-direction is given by \(v_x = x^2\) and the density varies as \(\rho = \frac{1}{x}\). Which of the following is a valid expression for the velocity component in the y-direction, \(v_y\)?
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Kinematics of Fluid Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Two-dimensional steady flow field
    • Velocity in x-direction: \(v_x = x^2\)
    • Density variation: \(\rho = \dfrac{1}{x}\)
  • Aim: Find a valid expression for the y-direction velocity component (\(v_y\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Continuity Equation for Compressible, Steady Flow: For steady 2D flow, conservation of mass requires: \[\frac{\partial(\rho v_x)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial(\rho v_y)}{\partial y} = 0 \] Since density \(\rho\) is not constant, it cannot be canceled out.

4. Solution Method:

Substitute given expressions for \(\rho\) and \(v_x\), evaluate the partial derivative w.r.t. \(x\), and integrate w.r.t. \(y\) to solve for \(v_y\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formulate mass flux in x-direction:
    \[\rho v_x = \left(\frac{1}{x}\right) x^2 = x \]
  2. Substitute into continuity equation:
    \[\frac{\partial(x)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\frac{1}{x} \cdot v_y\right) = 0 \]\[1 + \frac{1}{x}\frac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} = 0 \]
    Note: \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) is treated as a constant when differentiating partially w.r.t. \(y\).
  3. Isolate the derivative of \(v_y\):
    \[\frac{1}{x}\frac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} = -1 \implies \frac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} = -x \]
  4. Integrate partially w.r.t. \(y\):
    \[v_y = -xy + f(x) \]
    where \(f(x)\) is an arbitrary function of \(x\). For the simplest flow field where \(f(x) = 0\): \(v_y = -xy\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(v_y = -xy\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: For steady incompressible flow through a closed-conduit of uniform cross-section, the direction of flow will always be:
options: from higher to lower piezometric head

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: from higher to lower piezometric head
structuredOptions.html: from higher to lower piezometric head

questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Fluid Dynamics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Steady incompressible flow
    • Closed conduit of uniform cross-section
  • Aim: Identify the hydraulic parameter that definitively decreases in the direction of flow.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Bernoulli's Equation with Head Loss: \[H_1 = H_2 + h_L \implies H_1 > H_2 \] where Total Head \(H = \dfrac{P}{\gamma} + Z + \dfrac{v^2}{2g}\)
  • Piezometric Head (\(h_p\)): \[h_p = \frac{P}{\gamma} + Z \]

4. Solution Method:

In a uniform conduit with incompressible flow, continuity requires constant velocity throughout. Analyze how this affects the total energy gradient.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Continuity for uniform cross-section:
    \[A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2 \implies v_1 = v_2 = v \]
    Velocity head \(\dfrac{v^2}{2g}\) is constant at all points.
  2. Energy equation between points 1 and 2:
    \[\left(\frac{P_1}{\gamma} + Z_1 + \frac{v^2}{2g}\right) - \left(\frac{P_2}{\gamma} + Z_2 + \frac{v^2}{2g}\right) = h_L \]
  3. Cancel constant velocity head:
    \[\left(\frac{P_1}{\gamma} + Z_1\right) - \left(\frac{P_2}{\gamma} + Z_2\right) = h_L > 0 \]\[(h_p)_1 - (h_p)_2 = h_L \]
    Since \(h_L > 0\) always, \((h_p)_1 > (h_p)_2\). Flow proceeds from higher to lower piezometric head.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: from higher to lower piezometric head  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A circular pipe has a diameter of 1 m, bed slope of 1 in 1000, and Manning’s roughness coefficient equal to 0.01. It may be treated as an open channel flow when it is flowing just full, i.e., the water level just touches the crest. The discharge in this condition is denoted by \(Q_{full}\). Similarly, the discharge when the pipe is flowing half-full, i.e., with a flow depth of 0.5 m, is denoted by \(Q_{half}\). The ratio \(Q_{full} / Q_{half}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Water Resources Engineering | Open Channel Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pipe diameter: \(D = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Bed slope: \(S = 1/1000\) (constant)
    • Manning's \(n = 0.01\) (constant)
    • Condition 1: Flowing just full (\(Q_{full}\)) — treated as open channel
    • Condition 2: Flowing half-full, depth = \(0.5\text{ m}\) (\(Q_{half}\))
  • Aim: Compute the ratio \(Q_{full} / Q_{half}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Manning's Equation: \[Q = \frac{1}{n} A R^{2/3} \sqrt{S} \] where \(R = A/P\) is the hydraulic radius. When a pipe flows just full as an open channel, atmospheric pressure acts at the crown and the entire perimeter is wetted (\(P = \pi D\)).

4. Solution Method:

Find \(A\), \(P\), and \(R\) for both configurations. Apply Manning's equation and compute the discharge ratio.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Just Full Flow (\(Q_{full}\)):
    \[A_{full} = \frac{\pi}{4}D^2, \quad P_{full} = \pi D \]\[R_{full} = \frac{A_{full}}{P_{full}} = \frac{\pi D^2/4}{\pi D} = \frac{D}{4} \]
  2. Half-Full Flow (\(Q_{half}\)):
    \[A_{half} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{4}D^2 = \frac{\pi}{8}D^2, \quad P_{half} = \frac{\pi D}{2} \]\[R_{half} = \frac{\pi D^2/8}{\pi D/2} = \frac{D}{4} \]
    Note: Both conditions share the identical hydraulic radius \(R = D/4\).
  3. Calculate the discharge ratio:
    Since \(R_{full} = R_{half}\), the \(R^{2/3}\) terms cancel:
    \[\frac{Q_{full}}{Q_{half}} = \frac{A_{full}}{A_{half}} = \frac{\pi D^2/4}{\pi D^2/8} = 2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
The two columns below show some parameters and their possible values.

ParameterValue
P – Gross Command AreaI – 100 hectares/cumec
Q – Permanent Wilting PointII – 6 °C
R – Duty of canal waterIII – 1000 hectares
S – Delta of wheatIV – 1000 cm
V – 40 cm
VI – 0.12

Which of the following options matches the parameters and the values correctly?
questions.explanation:
Irrigation Engineering | Water Requirements of Crops

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Parameters (P, Q, R, S) to be matched with field values/units (I to VI).
  • Aim: Pair each parameter to its correct field value using unit taxonomy.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Gross Command Area (GCA): Total geographical area bounding the irrigation system. (Unit: Area)
  • Permanent Wilting Point (PWP): Minimum moisture level at which plants can no longer extract water from soil. (Unit: dimensionless fraction or %)
  • Duty: Land area irrigated per unit discharge over the base period. (Unit: Area/Discharge)
  • Delta (\(\Delta\)): Total depth of water needed by crop during entire growing season. (Unit: Length)

4. Solution Method:

Match each parameter to the option whose dimensions and typical values align with the definition.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • P — Gross Command Area: Requires an area. Option III (1000 hectares) fits. → P – III
  • Q — Permanent Wilting Point: Requires a moisture fraction. Option VI (0.12) represents 12% moisture. → Q – VI
  • R — Duty of canal water: Requires Area/Discharge. Option I (100 hectares/cumec) fits. → R – I
  • S — Delta of wheat: Requires depth (length). Option V (40 cm) fits the standard requirement for wheat. → S – V

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P-III, Q-VI, R-I, S-V  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: Two reservoirs are connected through a 930 m long, 0.3 m diameter pipe, which has a gate valve. The pipe entrance is sharp (loss coefficient = 0.5) and the valve is half-open (loss coefficient = 5.5). The head difference between the two reservoirs is 20 m. Assume the friction factor for the pipe as 0.03 and \(g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2\). The discharge in the pipe accounting for all minor and major losses is __________ m³/s.
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Pipe Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Length: \(L = 930\text{ m}\), Diameter: \(D = 0.3\text{ m}\)
    • Head difference: \(H = 20\text{ m}\)
    • Friction factor: \(f = 0.03\), Gravity: \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Minor loss coefficients: Entrance \(K_{ent} = 0.5\), Valve \(K_{val} = 5.5\)
  • Aim: Compute the discharge \(Q\) in m³/s accounting for major and minor losses.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Apply Energy Conservation between two reservoirs.
  • Total head loss: \(H = h_{friction} + \sum h_{minor}\)
  • Minor losses include entrance, valve, and exit loss (standard exit loss \(K_{exit} = 1.0\)).
  • \[H = \left(\frac{fL}{D} + K_{ent} + K_{val} + K_{exit}\right)\frac{V^2}{2g} \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the Head Loss Equation:
    \[K_{total} = \frac{0.03 \times 930}{0.3} + 0.5 + 5.5 + 1.0 = 93 + 7 = 100 \]\[20 = 100 \times \frac{V^2}{2 \times 10} \implies 20 = 5V^2 \]
  2. Solve for Velocity:
    \[V^2 = \frac{20}{5} = 4 \implies V = 2\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Calculate Discharge:
    \[A = \frac{\pi}{4}(0.3)^2 = 0.070686\text{ m}^2 \]\[Q = A \times V = 0.070686 \times 2 = 0.14137\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.141 m³/s  |  Accepted key range: 0.140 to 0.142

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A hydraulic jump is formed in a 2 m wide rectangular channel which is horizontal and frictionless. The post-jump depth and velocity are 0.8 m and 1 m/s, respectively. The pre-jump velocity is __________ m/s. (use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (Hydraulic Jump)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Rectangular channel, width \(B = 2\text{ m}\), \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Post-jump variables: depth \(y_2 = 0.8\text{ m}\), velocity \(V_2 = 1\text{ m/s}\)
  • Aim: Find the pre-jump velocity \(V_1\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Unit Discharge Continuity: \(q = y_1 V_1 = y_2 V_2\)
  • Conjugate Depth Relationship for rectangular channel: \[y_1 = \frac{y_2}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8\,Fr_2^2} - 1\right) \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find unit discharge \(q\) and \(Fr_2^2\):
    \[q = y_2 V_2 = 0.8 \times 1 = 0.8\text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]\[Fr_2^2 = \frac{V_2^2}{g\,y_2} = \frac{1^2}{10 \times 0.8} = \frac{1}{8} = 0.125 \]
  2. Find pre-jump depth \(y_1\):
    \[y_1 = \frac{0.8}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8(0.125)} - 1\right) = 0.4\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right) \]\[y_1 = 0.4 \times (1.4142 - 1) = 0.4 \times 0.4142 = 0.16568\text{ m} \]
  3. Calculate \(V_1\):
    \[V_1 = \frac{q}{y_1} = \frac{0.8}{0.16568} = 4.828\text{ m/s} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.83 m/s  |  Accepted key range: 4.75 to 4.85

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A short reach of a 2 m wide rectangular open channel has its bed level rising in the direction of flow at a slope of 1 in 10000. It carries a discharge of 4 m³/s and its Manning’s roughness coefficient is 0.01. The flow in this reach is gradually varying. At a certain section in this reach, the depth of flow was measured as 0.5 m. The rate of change of the water depth with distance, dy/dx, at this section is __________ (use g = 10 m/s²).
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (Gradually Varied Flow)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Channel width: \(B = 2\text{ m}\)
    • Bed slope rises → \(S_0 = -1/10000 = -0.0001\) (negative: adverse slope)
    • Discharge: \(Q = 4\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\), Manning's \(n = 0.01\)
    • Measured depth: \(y = 0.5\text{ m}\), \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Determine the rate of change of depth \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • GVF Dynamic Equation: \[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{S_0 - S_f}{1 - Fr^2} \]
  • Froude Number: \(Fr^2 = \dfrac{V^2}{g\,y}\)
  • Friction Slope (Manning's): \[S_f = \left(\frac{n\,Q}{A\,R^{2/3}}\right)^2 \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Geometric Parameters:
    \[A = 2 \times 0.5 = 1.0\text{ m}^2, \quad P = 2 + 2(0.5) = 3.0\text{ m} \]\[R = \frac{1.0}{3.0} = 0.3333\text{ m} \implies R^{2/3} = 0.4807 \]
  2. Calculate Velocity and \(Fr^2\):
    \[V = \frac{Q}{A} = \frac{4}{1.0} = 4\text{ m/s} \]\[Fr^2 = \frac{4^2}{10 \times 0.5} = \frac{16}{5} = 3.2 \]
  3. Calculate Friction Slope (\(S_f\)):
    \[S_f = \left(\frac{0.01 \times 4}{1.0 \times 0.4807}\right)^2 = (0.08320)^2 = 0.006922 \]
  4. Determine \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\):
    \[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{-0.0001 - 0.006922}{1 - 3.2} = \frac{-0.007022}{-2.2} = 0.003192 \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.00319  |  Accepted key range: 0.0031 to 0.0033

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The drag force, \(F_D\), on a sphere kept in a uniform flow field depends on the diameter of the sphere, D; flow velocity, V; fluid density, \(\rho\); and dynamic viscosity, \(\mu\). Which of the following options represents the non-dimensional parameters which could be used to analyze this problem?
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Dimensional Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data: Variables — Drag force \(F_D\), diameter \(D\), velocity \(V\), density \(\rho\), dynamic viscosity \(\mu\).
  • Aim: Identify the correct non-dimensional parameters (Pi terms) matching the options.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Buckingham Pi Theorem:
    • Total variables: \(n = 5\) (\(F_D, D, V, \rho, \mu\))
    • Fundamental dimensions: \(m = 3\) (\(M, L, T\))
    • Number of \(\Pi\) terms \(= n - m = 5 - 3 = 2\)
  • Repeating variables selected: \(\rho, D, V\) (representing density, geometry, and kinematics).

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. First \(\Pi\) term (using \(F_D\)):
    Dimensions: \([F_D] = MLT^{-2}\), \([\rho] = ML^{-3}\), \([V] = LT^{-1}\), \([D] = L\)
    Standard drag coefficient formulation:
    \[\Pi_1 = \frac{F_D}{\rho V^2 D^2} \]
    Verification: \(\dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{(ML^{-3})(L^2T^{-2})(L^2)} = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{MLT^{-2}} = 1\) ✓
  2. Second \(\Pi\) term (using \(\mu\)):
    Dimensions: \([\mu] = ML^{-1}T^{-1}\)
    Standard Reynolds Number formulation:
    \[\Pi_2 = \frac{\rho V D}{\mu} \]
    Verification: \(\dfrac{(ML^{-3})(LT^{-1})(L)}{ML^{-1}T^{-1}} = \dfrac{ML^{-1}T^{-1}}{ML^{-1}T^{-1}} = 1\) ✓
  3. Check given Options:
    Option (C) matches perfectly: \(\dfrac{F_D}{\rho V^2 D^2}\) and \(\dfrac{\rho V D}{\mu}\)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Option (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: In a catchment, there are four rain-gauge stations, P, Q, R, and S. Normal annual precipitation values at these stations are 780 mm, 850 mm, 920 mm, and 980 mm, respectively. In the year 2013, stations Q, R, and S, were operative but P was not. Using the normal ratio method, the precipitation at station P for the year 2013 has been estimated as 860 mm. If the observed precipitation at stations Q and R for the year 2013 were 930 mm and 1010 mm, respectively; what was the observed precipitation (in mm) at station S for that year?
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Precipitation & Missing Data Estimation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    StationNormal Annual Precipitation (mm)Observed 2013 Precipitation (mm)
    P (missing)\(N_P = 780\)\(P_P = 860\) (estimated)
    Q\(N_Q = 850\)\(P_Q = 930\)
    R\(N_R = 920\)\(P_R = 1010\)
    S\(N_S = 980\)\(P_S = ?\)
  • Aim: Find the observed precipitation at station S (\(P_S\)) for 2013.

3. Core Concepts:

Normal Ratio Method: When the normal annual precipitation of index stations differs by more than 10% from the missing station, the Normal Ratio Method is used: \[P_P = \frac{N_P}{m}\left(\frac{P_Q}{N_Q} + \frac{P_R}{N_R} + \frac{P_S}{N_S}\right) \] where \(m = 3\) is the number of index stations.

4. Solution Method:

Substitute known values into the Normal Ratio Method formula and solve linearly for \(P_S\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Setup the equation:
    \[860 = \frac{780}{3}\left(\frac{930}{850} + \frac{1010}{920} + \frac{P_S}{980}\right) \]
  2. Simplify constants:
    \[860 = 260\left(1.09412 + 1.09783 + \frac{P_S}{980}\right) \]
  3. Isolate the bracket:
    \[\frac{860}{260} = 2.19195 + \frac{P_S}{980} \]\[3.30769 = 2.19195 + \frac{P_S}{980} \]
  4. Solve for \(P_S\):
    \[\frac{P_S}{980} = 3.30769 - 2.19195 = 1.11574 \]\[P_S = 1.11574 \times 980 = 1093.43\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1093.43 mm  |  Accepted key range: 1093 to 1094
